children: The Reserve Bank of Australia has been setting the stage for an interest-rate increase this week for some time. A 25 basis-point hike seems locked in, with the central bank set to highlight upside risks to inflation and the unresolved war in the Middle East. It's the RBA's use of language that will be key. The bank clearly has doubts that it can achieve its inflation target within a reasonable time frame and is now putting less emphasis on protecting jobs. The RBA's rhetoric is likely to be direct, keeping the door open to a further hike in November. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)
